new_entities.name: Methotrexate with folic acid supplementation
new_entities.description: Methotrexate treatment accompanied by routine folic acid or folinic acid supplementation to reduce toxicity.

new_entities.name: Reduction in adverse events
new_entities.description: Lower frequency or severity of treatment-related adverse effects during methotrexate therapy.

edges.effect_quant: The Cochrane review found a 26% relative reduction in gastrointestinal side effects with folate supplementation, while an earlier meta-analysis found an OR of 0.21 for mucosal and GI toxicity with folic acid.
edges.population: adults receiving low-dose methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis and other chronic inflammatory diseases
edges.mechanism: Folic acid replenishes folate-dependent pathways partially suppressed by methotrexate, reducing collateral injury in mucosal, hepatic, and hematologic tissues without meaningfully abolishing the intended anti-inflammatory effect in most studies.
edges.summary: Adding folic acid to low-dose methotrexate reduces clinically important toxicity and is one of the best-supported mitigation strategies in routine rheumatology practice. The signal is strongest for mucosal, gastrointestinal, and liver-related adverse effects rather than for every toxicity domain equally.
edges.caveats: Some analyses discuss a theoretical tradeoff between folate rescue and methotrexate efficacy, but most modern evidence finds the toxicity benefit dominates and routine co-prescription remains standard. Exact benefit magnitude differs by dose, schedule, and whether folic or folinic acid is used.

evidence.citation: Shea B et al 2013 Cochrane Database Syst Rev
evidence.notes: Folic acid and folinic acid for reducing side effects in patients receiving methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis.

effect_quant.comparator: gastrointestinal side effects with folate supplementation versus placebo or no folate

evidence.citation: Ortiz Z et al 1998 J Rheumatol
evidence.notes: The efficacy of folic acid and folinic acid in reducing methotrexate gastrointestinal toxicity in rheumatoid arthritis. A metaanalysis of randomized controlled trials.

effect_quant.comparator: mucosal and gastrointestinal toxicity with folic acid supplementation versus placebo or no folate

evidence.citation: Mazaud C et al 2017 Br J Dermatol
evidence.notes: Relative risk of and determinants for adverse events of methotrexate prescribed at a low dose: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized placebo-controlled trials.
